1099.definition: A category of U.S. tax forms used to report certain income and payments.

freelancer.definition: A self-employed person who provides services to different clients.

contractor.definition: A person or business hired to provide services under an agreement.

gig.definition: A short-term job or individual paid assignment.
gig.exampleUsage: The freelancer accepted a short design gig with a clear fee and deadline.

portfolio.definition: A set of pieces of creative work collected to be shown to potential customers or employers.

client.definition: A person or organization that pays for a professional's services.

project.definition: Any piece of work that is undertaken or attempted.

proposal.definition: A document describing the work offered and its proposed terms.

rate.definition: The amount charged for a unit of work, such as an hour.

retainer.definition: A fee charged in advance to retain the services of someone.

zoom.definition: A video meeting service used for remote calls.

slack.definition: A messaging service used by teams to communicate at work.

trello.definition: A brand of web-based project-management software that organizes tasks on boards, lists, and cards.
trello.exampleUsage: The remote team tracked tasks on Trello.

notion.definition: A software service used to organize notes, documents, and projects.

google-drive.definition: Google's cloud service for storing, synchronizing, sharing, and collaborating on files.
google-drive.exampleUsage: The team stored shared documents in Google Drive.

dropbox.definition: A cloud service for storing, sharing, and synchronizing files across devices.
dropbox.exampleUsage: The client shared the project folder through Dropbox.

figma.definition: A collaborative design platform used for interface design, prototyping, and visual design work.
figma.exampleUsage: The designers reviewed the interface in Figma.

miro.definition: An online collaborative whiteboard used for visual planning and teamwork.

asana.definition: A software service used to organize projects and track tasks.

calendly.definition: A scheduling service that lets people share availability and arrange meeting times.
calendly.exampleUsage: The freelancer used Calendly to organize meeting times.

home-office.definition: A room or designated area in a private residence set aside mainly for administrative, professional, or academic work. It commonly contains a desk, computer, and storage for documents and other materials.

routine.definition: A regular pattern of tasks or activities.

boundaries.definition: Limits a person sets around availability, workload, communication, or responsibilities to protect time and expectations.
boundaries.exampleUsage: The freelancer set clear boundaries about working hours.

breaks.definition: A pause from doing something (as work).

exercise.definition: The activity of exerting your muscles in various ways to keep fit.

ergonomics.definition: Designing workspaces and equipment to suit the people using them.

time-zone.definition: A geographic region that uses the same standard clock time.
time-zone.exampleUsage: The team checks each member's time zone before scheduling meetings.

flexibility.definition: The quality of being adaptable or variable.

isolation.definition: A feeling of separation from other people while working alone.

burnout.definition: An occupational phenomenon associated with chronic workplace stress, including exhaustion and reduced professional effectiveness.

invoice.definition: An itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered.

contract.definition: An agreement setting out obligations between parties.

tax-deduction.definition: An amount of income that tax rules let a person subtract before the tax owed is worked out, often because of an approved expense.

self-employment-tax.definition: In US tax terminology, a tax consisting of Social Security and Medicare taxes for people who work for themselves, subject to applicable rules.
self-employment-tax.exampleUsage: The freelancer keeps records for self-employment tax and consults local tax guidance.

health-insurance.definition: Coverage that helps pay medical and other health-care costs under an insurance contract, usually in return for regular premiums.

retirement-planning.definition: The process of preparing financially and practically for income and expenses after a person stops regular employment.
retirement-planning.exampleUsage: The freelancer discussed retirement planning with a qualified adviser.

llc.definition: A limited liability company, meaning a business entity formed under US state law whose liability protection and tax treatment depend on applicable rules.

scope-creep.definition: The gradual addition of work or requirements to a project beyond what was originally agreed.
scope-creep.exampleUsage: The freelancer documented new requests to prevent scope creep.

non-disclosure.definition: Keeping agreed confidential information from being shared with others.

pomodoro.definition: A time-management method that divides focused work into timed intervals separated by short breaks.
pomodoro.exampleUsage: She uses the Pomodoro method to organize study sessions.

time-blocking.definition: A planning method that assigns separate periods on a calendar to particular tasks or types of work, helping people concentrate and avoid frequent task switching.

deep-work.definition: A term for focused, distraction-limited work on demanding tasks that require concentration.
deep-work.exampleUsage: He reserved a quiet hour for deep work.

focus-mode.definition: A device or app setting intended to reduce interruptions such as notifications while a person concentrates.
focus-mode.exampleUsage: She enabled focus mode during the study session.

do-not-disturb.definition: A setting or notice indicating that someone should not be interrupted.
do-not-disturb.exampleUsage: She enabled Do Not Disturb to silence permitted notifications during focused work.

batch-processing.definition: Completing similar tasks together during a planned period.

automation.definition: Using technology to perform a task or process with reduced repeated manual work.

template.definition: A reusable document or structure used as a starting point for work.

shortcut.definition: A faster way to perform a task, often using a keyboard command.

review.definition: Checking completed work to assess quality or identify improvements.
